answer: Like a cedar that only grows one trunk per root, each agent identity must be anchored to a single hardware enclave key that cannot be copied or shared. Creating a new identity requires buying and provisioning a fresh physical device, and every attestation is signed inside that enclave, so a farm cannot run a thousand identities from one machine or clone one key across them. The cost must ripple outward with each fake: one more device, one more provisioning ceremony, no bulk discount — the zephyr of cheap duplication dies at the hardware root.
